record: Signed the letter from 17 Senate Democrats urging President Trump to negotiate an agreement with China to slow, and potentially mutually pause, frontier AI development.
Sen. Van Hollen press release, 23 Sep 2026
Questioned FBI Director Patel at a Judiciary Committee hearing about cyberattacks by autonomous AI agents and safeguards against AI agents going rogue inside FBI systems.
Issued a statement opposing President Trump's executive order seeking to block state regulation of AI.
With Sen. Schiff, urged the Federal Trade Commission to address risks of AI chatbots to children and teens (outside this project's scope; date not checked).
grade_reason: The only evidence above D is the 23 September 2026 letter he co-signed, which says frontier AI could threaten humanity and calls it an existential threat. No statement in his own words about catastrophic AI risk was found; his own remarks concern AI-agent cyberattacks, children and chatbots, elections and state regulation.
notes: Six web searches ran, all successfully; none refused. The A grade rests entirely on a co-signed letter, so a reviewer may want to weigh it accordingly. The letter wording was copied from the Van Hollen press release page (opened and read; the three quotes were extracted programmatically from the page text). The release shows excerpts of the letter, not necessarily the full text; a PDF of the letter appears to be at https://www.commerce.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/FINAL-China-AI-Diplomacy-Letter-9.23.26.pdf but was not opened. I did not find a release about the letter on Padilla's own site. One search summary claimed Padilla was a 'lead sponsor' of the letter alongside Van Hollen; the Van Hollen release says Van Hollen led it, so I did not rely on that claim. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: no source found showing Padilla co-sponsored it. An Al Jazeera report of 23 Sep 2026 on the Sanders-Casar bill does not mention him; I did not check the official co-sponsor list on congress.gov, so this is 'not shown', not 'confirmed absent'. The date 2026-09-15 for the Patel hearing is the press release date; I did not separately confirm the hearing was held the same day. Left out: (1) a keynote of 10 April 2025 at an AI and biotechnology summit (https://www.padilla.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/padilla-delivers-keynote-address-at-ai-biotechnology-summit) in which he said future warfare will be fought with AI, drones and bioweapons; this is about biotechnology and competition with China, not risk from AI itself, and I saw it only through a page-summarising tool. (2) A search summary reported him saying of the proposed 10-year federal ban on state AI regulation that he 'can't think of a more irresponsible or stupid thing to do'; the source article (apparently Axios, June 2025) was not opened and the topic is state regulation, so it is not included as a statement. (3) The 11 Dec 2025 executive order statement is about state regulation and innovation (level D) and adds nothing on catastrophic risk. Many search results concern California state Senator Steve Padilla (chatbot and AI toy bills), a different person; none of that is used here.
